fields.method: Same Gaia/MCPS catalogues, selection, completeness and physical smoothing. Native positions are redeposited on the grid specified by n. Component budgets, warp, dust, objects, stars, heights and grades are unchanged.

numericalSampling.objectQuadrature: 4 by 4 subpixel chords, analytic finite-object columns and positive depth quadrature. Unresolved stars retain their original bilinear point rasterization.
numericalSampling.optimizationReplay: 128 px complete frames before and after numerical acceleration agree exactly in three views and to an absolute difference of 1.3e-23 in edge-on. No finite object or its foreground dust is clipped.
numericalSampling.tiling: Each tile retains the complete camera and complete-object flux normalization. A behavior test proves assembled masked tiles equal the complete projection. Six workers, ten-minute job deadline and complete tile receipts.

milkyWay.qualification: These saved errors compare axis-local unmerged RGBA with the spectral field. They are not a delivered near-station tolerance. Benchmark the installed merged bank at matched near cameras before judging the LMC.

interpretation: The larger outside field of view was a major presentation difference. Finer native catalogue grids and ray sampling preserve the accepted Earth calibration. At the Earth horizontal physical pixel pitch, finite knots and resolved stellar grain remain sharp from the outside. The remaining view-dependent smoothness includes genuine integration through the adopted physical thicknesses; resolution convergence is not a measurement of the unknown far side.
limitations: Native processing reuses the accepted local catalogue and map caches; this is not a cache-free input-recovery qualification. No new physical structure, photometric fit, slab bake or site installation is claimed by this model-resolution record.
